background_notes.fact: For ordinary metric spaces X,Y, d((x,y),(x',y'))=max(d_X(x,x'),d_Y(y,y')) is a metric on X×Y. Ordinary metrics induce extended metrics by viewing each finite nonnegative distance in [0,∞]; any map preserving all ordinary distances also preserves these extended distances.

grounds.reason: Rn(n) has its stated Euclidean metric, including the one-point case n=0.
The real line carries its usual metric.
The ambient product distance is explicitly the maximum of the two coordinate distances.
S002 computes equality of the ordinary distances for every real pair t,u.

background_notes.justification: Nonnegativity, symmetry and separation for the maximum follow from those of each coordinate metric. Each coordinate distance between a first and third point is bounded by the sum of the two corresponding product distances, so their maximum obeys the triangle inequality. Embedding the resulting finite distances into [0,∞] preserves the metric axioms and the distance equalities computed in S002.
